title: Investigating the Impact of LLM Personality on Cognitive Bias Manifestation in Automated Decision-Making Tasks

bias_targets.methodology: Evaluating how prior decisions influence subsequent admission choices using paired synthetic student profiles where one decision precedes another.
Comparing LLM admission rates for identical student profiles when the prompt uses positive ('Would you admit') versus negative ('Would reject') framing.
Measuring the selection rate difference between an option framed as the default (e.g., a candidate previously worked with) and neutral alternative options.
Measuring shifts in target option preferences when an asymmetrically dominated 'decoy' option is introduced in multi-choice selection tasks.
Quantifying the preference for certain outcomes over probabilistic ones by evaluating choices under loss versus gain framing.
Evaluating the likelihood of an LLM favoring continued investment in failing endeavors when prior investments are present compared to a baseline with no sunk costs.
Comparing the LLM-assigned monetary value of items when they are presented as 'owned' by the user versus when they are unowned or considered for purchase.

Testing for group attribution bias by presenting identical student profiles that differ only by a gender attribute to see if classification rates (e.g., assessing if a student is 'good at math') change.
